questions.stem: Which cervical plexus block technique carries risk of intrathecal or vertebral artery injection?
Why is the superficial cervical plexus block preferred over the deep block?
questions.answer: Simpler and safer, and suits most indications

questions.stem: Which spinal nerve roots form the cervical plexus?
In the cervical plexus, which nerve is carried mainly by loop 1 (C1–C2)?
Which nerves make up loop 2 (C2–C3) of the cervical plexus?
questions.answer: Ansa cervicalis, greater auricular and transverse cervical nerves

questions.stem: Which nerve is carried by loop 3 (C3–C4) of the cervical plexus?
How many cutaneous branches does the superficial cervical plexus have?
Which root supplies the lesser occipital nerve of the superficial cervical plexus?
Which roots supply the greater auricular nerve of the cervical plexus?
Which roots supply the transverse cervical nerve of the cervical plexus?
Which roots supply the supraclavicular nerve of the cervical plexus?
In the cervical plexus, where do the four superficial branches emerge relative to the SCM?
questions.answer: From behind the posterior border of the SCM

questions.stem: What sensory skin territory does the superficial cervical plexus supply?
questions.answer: Anterolateral neck, from jawline to clavicle, back to the mastoid

questions.stem: Which muscle receives motor supply from the deep cervical plexus?
Which nerves does a cervical plexus block not cover?
options: Lesser occipital and greater auricular nerves
Ansa cervicalis and transverse cervical nerves

questions.stem: For a superficial cervical plexus block, at which layer is local anaesthetic deposited?
options: Superficial to the deep cervical fascia
Between the investing fascia and prevertebral fascia

questions.stem: The intermediate cervical plexus block injects between the investing layer of deep cervical fascia and the ____
For a deep cervical plexus block, where is local anaesthetic deposited?
options: Superficial to the deep cervical fascia

questions.stem: In the landmark superficial cervical plexus block, where is the first subcutaneous infiltration made?
options: Lateral to the C4 transverse process
Midpoint of the posterior SCM border

questions.stem: In the landmark superficial cervical plexus block fan technique, how far above and below the insertion point do you redirect?
In the landmark superficial cervical plexus block, how much local anaesthetic goes in at the midpoint?
In the landmark superficial cervical plexus block, what volume is given caudad and cephalad along the posterior border?
In the landmark superficial cervical plexus block, how deep should the injection stay?
options: Up to 5 cm into the neck

questions.stem: What is the total local anaesthetic volume for the landmark superficial cervical plexus block?
Given that no motor block is needed, which ropivacaine concentration suits the landmark superficial cervical plexus block?
In the ultrasound true superficial cervical plexus block, where is subcutaneous infiltration made?
Which procedure is an indication for the intermediate cervical plexus block?
What advantages does ultrasound give over landmarks for the intermediate cervical plexus block?
questions.answer: See the spread in the right plane, avoid going too deep and hitting nearby structures

questions.stem: For the ultrasound intermediate cervical plexus block, local anaesthetic should reach the sensory branches of which nerves?
Which needle length is used for the ultrasound intermediate cervical plexus block?
For the ultrasound intermediate cervical plexus block, what volume of local anaesthetic is used?
Which local anaesthetic concentration suits the purely sensory intermediate cervical plexus block?
When injecting an intermediate cervical plexus block under ultrasound, what should you see, and what if spread is poor?
questions.answer: Layering out between the SCM and prevertebral fascia; reposition if spread is poor

questions.stem: For the intermediate cervical plexus block, if the plexus is not seen, which alternative approach is used?
When doing an ultrasound intermediate cervical plexus block, which vessels should you look for?
What does the deep cervical plexus block effectively amount to, and at which roots?
questions.answer: A paravertebral block of C2–C4 at the intervertebral foramina

questions.stem: In the landmark deep cervical plexus block, which line is drawn to locate the insertion points?
questions.answer: From the mastoid tip to Chassaignac's tubercle

questions.stem: In the landmark deep cervical plexus block, how far caudal to the mastoid is the C4 insertion point?
In the landmark deep cervical plexus block, how far caudal to the mastoid is the C3 insertion point?
What injection options are described for the deep cervical plexus block?
questions.answer: Single injection at C4, or triple injection at C2, C3 and C4

questions.stem: For the deep cervical plexus block, how much local anaesthetic is given per level?
In the FRCA landmark deep cervical plexus technique, where is local anaesthetic infiltrated?
questions.answer: Lateral to the transverse processes of the second, third and fourth cervical vertebrae, about 2 cm deep

questions.stem: How do complications of the superficial and intermediate cervical plexus blocks compare with interscalene block?
options: Much higher, with frequent phrenic palsy
Similar, with serious complications close to zero
Lower, with no reported nerve injury

questions.stem: Compared with the superficial cervical plexus block, how do complications of the deep cervical plexus block compare?
What conversion-to-general-anaesthesia rate is quoted for the cervical plexus block?
